chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about two chickens that were fattened, which I slaughtered while I was in Makkah. So he said to me: 'Why did you slaughter them?' I said: 'A slave girl from the people of Makkah came to me with them and asked me to slaughter them, so I thought I was in al-Kufa and did not remember the Sanctuary (al-Haram).' So he said: 'Upon you is their price.' I said: 'How much is their price?' He said: 'One dirham, and it is better than them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for mistakenly hunting in the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of 'ghafla' (heedlessness) versus 'jahla' (ignorance), where the Imam distinguishes between a mistake in location while knowing the rule versus a lack of knowledge of the rule itself. By assessing the value at one dirham and declaring it 'better than the animal,' Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the spiritual merit of expiation over mere compensation, a nuance often discussed in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the nature of fidya. This ruling serves as a foundational precedent for calculating the value of hunted game in the Haram, emphasizing the sanctity of the precincts even in cases of unintentional violation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan and Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about two chickens which I slaughtered and I was in Makkah. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Why did you slaughter them?’ So I said, ‘A slave girl from the people of Makkah came with these two to me and asked me to slaughter them. So I thought I was in Al-Kufa and I did not remember the Al-Harram’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon you is their price’. I said, ‘How much is their price?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘One Dirham, and it is better than these two’.
en.sarwar: 21. Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from and Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of my slaughtering two fledgling birds in Makkah. He (the Imam) said, ‘Did you slaughter them?’ I replied, ‘Yes, because a slave-girl of the people of Makkah brought them to me and asked me to slaughter them and I thought I was in al-Kufah and did not remember al-Haram (the sacred area). He (the Imam) said, ‘You must pay their price.’ I asked, ‘How much is it?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is one dirham and it is better than them.’”
